f4b4bb981e:c51e5baede298a64.summary: Ancona was born from geography: a promontory that bends into the sea, a natural feature that the ancients recognized and called "Ankón," the "elbow" of Italy. It is a shape that embodies both function and metaphor: shelter and openness, protection and horizon.

f4b4bb981e:d0e1f30ecc70a48f.summary: The project, developed in collaboration with the Adam Mickiewicz Institute (IAM) team and the Culture.pl editorial team, aimed to build relationships with artists and creative communities (IAM visual identity) and present Polish culture and its creators to an international audience (Culture.pl). IAM works with artists and people in the cultural sector who think outside the box, experiment, challenge existing ideas and take risks. We wanted the Institute's visual identity to reflect this open and bold approach, while giving space to the work itself. Rather than compete with the artists' work for attention, the visual identity provides a clear, distinctive and flexible frame for presenting it.

f4b4bb981e:855b9ca3ae3840bf.title: Terrifying True Tales
f4b4bb981e:855b9ca3ae3840bf.summary: A few of the interior illustrations I did for Terrifying True Tales for National Geographic in 2025.

f4b4bb981e:45a9357592e12b67.title: Where You Stand Shapes What You Can See
f4b4bb981e:45a9357592e12b67.summary: Our experiences, assumptions, and emotions influence how we see the world. The same moment can hold different meanings depending on who is looking, where they stand, and what they bring with them.

f4b4bb981e:c911b390534d0537.title: Aether Scent
f4b4bb981e:c911b390534d0537.summary: A quiet bloom of botanical resonance, unfolding across seven living species. Aether Scent is a studio exploration of nature through a digital lens. An imagined collection of botanical essences in which every specimen moves between the familiar and the unknown, retaining traces of its organic origin while growing into something new.

f4b4bb981e:cd8abe45d7552823.title: Mascot Collection
f4b4bb981e:cd8abe45d7552823.summary: Meet Flowy, Glowy, and Peanut! Three little characters with their own personalities, looks, and stories. We had fun creating this collection and exploring different emotions, poses, and ways to bring these guys into apps, social media, and branding. Hope you enjoy them as much as we do!

f4b4bb981e:c460ad19d835a4f4.title: Noche en Blanco Málaga 2026
f4b4bb981e:c460ad19d835a4f4.summary: LNEB es un evento dedicado a la creación cultural en Málaga, que acoge actividades, exposiciones y propuestas artísticas abiertas al público. Esta edición se desarrolla bajo el lema "El futuro se escribe con música", una temática que toma la música como punto de partida para conectar cultura, innovación y participación ciudadana. Para su identidad visual nos hemos inspirado en el movimiento y la vibración del sonido. La propuesta se construye a partir de una tipografía variable y un sistema gráfico vivo, capaz de transformarse y reaccionar a la música. Las formas circulares que componen las letras hacen referencia a los ciclos lunares, conectando visualmente con el imaginario del evento. El sistema visual se expande mediante texturas, deformaciones y animaciones influenciadas por el Op Art, utilizando colores vibrantes y contrastados que refuerzan el carácter del evento. La identidad busca convertirse en una experiencia dinámica e interactiva.

f4b4bb981e:ec58974820919c94.title: TIDAL SCULPTURES ? Iceland
f4b4bb981e:ec58974820919c94.summary: Temporary sand islands in a lagoon on Iceland's east coast, shaped by wind, tides, and rain. Low evening light reveals sculptural ridges, dark textures, and cool blue water.

f4b4bb981e:a363c7135b5c591b.title: Farseer
f4b4bb981e:a363c7135b5c591b.summary: Farseer is a financial planning platform built around a spreadsheet interface, giving finance teams a familiar environment with high-performance technology underneath. The brand was built on the same principle. Spreadsheets became the foundation of the identity system, shaped into a visual language that feels lighter, faster, and more human than traditional finance software. When a product changes the way people work, it changes the way they feel about work too. We rebuilt Farseer across verbal identity, visual identity, motion, audio, sub-brands, and a new website.

f4b4bb981e:b3a821c5df2d9011.title: Tiempos inciertos
f4b4bb981e:b3a821c5df2d9011.summary: Visual identity and graphic communication system for Tiempos inciertos (Uncertain Times), the international congress organised by ADACE, the Spanish Association of Contemporary Art Directors, held at the Federico García Lorca Centre in Granada. The event reflects on the present and future of cultural institutions, addressing issues such as governance, collections, sustainability, new technologies and audiences. The graphic proposal builds on ADACE's distinctive yellow underline, a recurring element of its visual identity, expanding it into a vibrant palette inspired by text highlighters. The title Tiempos inciertos is partially obscured by the bands themselves, evoking a present marked by uncertainty, in which everything seems to be under review and in search of balance.

f4b4bb981e:61c3db0238d957c7.title: OTZ LAB
f4b4bb981e:61c3db0238d957c7.summary: OTZ LAB is OTEYZA's unisex fragrance collection. We designed the bottle, packaging and visual identity to translate the brand's dialogue between tradition and the avant-garde into perfumery. The bottle pairs the solidity of matte black steel with the fragility of glass, shaped like a test tube to evoke experimentation. A sphere in distinctive colours and textures identifies each fragrance, while the boxes feature compositions inspired by constructivism. A design that reinterprets traditional perfume packaging through structure, material and intention.

f4b4bb981e:0bcd3a79518fc6fb.title: Came from the stars
f4b4bb981e:0bcd3a79518fc6fb.summary: Another installment of the creative project exploring new Carpathian myths. Illustrations inspired by Hutsul folklore and Carpathian cultural aesthetics.

f4b4bb981e:e51d7a75dde3cf12.title: Shania Twain for the Sunday Times

f4b4bb981e:8ff2934edd02d3de.title: Piega
f4b4bb981e:8ff2934edd02d3de.summary: PIEGA is a brand direction for a women's label built on the fold. The symbol is a paper pentagon folded into seven pieces. The logo prints itself in reverse, the way wet ink does when you fold a page. Every garment keeps a red the street never sees: a lining, a hem tape, the back of a fold.

f4b4bb981e:7de9560f4ddf0c63.title: Our very first painting exhibition
f4b4bb981e:7de9560f4ddf0c63.summary: This exhibition explores the meaning of space and place through personal experiences and memories. Each individual shapes their own environment over time, turning it into more than just a physical setting. Everyday moments, like sitting on a chair or drinking water, become part of a deeper emotional landscape.

f4b4bb981e:bdad977510edfa7e.title: Quantum Security Brand Identity & Pitch Deck
f4b4bb981e:bdad977510edfa7e.summary: Quantum Deep is a deep-tech company building probabilistic computing hardware for cybersecurity, semiconductors, and post-quantum cryptography. Ahead of a new funding round, they came to us for a brand identity mature enough to match their technology and win the confidence of investors and enterprise customers. We built the full brand foundation: strategy, tone of voice, and a complete visual system with logo, typography, and color. Rather than leaning on generic quantum clichés, we designed a graphic language rooted in probability, photonics, and structured uncertainty. It scales across every touchpoint, from the website and investor pitch decks to 3D product visualization of the chip, brand guidelines, social, and events. A credible, category-defining identity for a B2B deep-tech brand, by Prznt Perfect.

f4b4bb981e:b376d07938fdff15.title: Portraits 2023-2026
f4b4bb981e:b376d07938fdff15.summary: A collection of hand-drawn digital portrait illustrations inspired by classical engraving, woodcut and traditional pen and ink techniques. The portraits were created for a variety of commercial and editorial projects, including advertising campaigns, corporate portraits, brand identity, packaging design, and commissioned artwork. Combining detailed linework, crosshatching, and a monochrome palette, these illustrations reinterpret the visual language of historical engraving in a contemporary digital medium.

f4b4bb981e:840a78a91f95502a.summary: Da San Chaek Gil is a brand representing the commercial and cultural district of Dasan New Town in Namyangju. Supported by the city government and the Regional Intellectual Property Center under the Korean Intellectual Property Office, FRONT KIT conducted its total branding including the naming which indicates "Da San (area) + San Chaek (stroll) + Chaek (book) + Gil (path)," that are the features of the district. Also, the project encompassed the creation of a comprehensive brand identity, including slogans, storytelling, characters, and application designs that reflect Dasan's vibrant scenery and cultural sentiment. Additionally, intellectual property rights were filed, workshops for merchants were conducted, and the geographic name was officially registered, ensuring a systematic and professional public branding. Da San Chaek Gil will offer a foundation for sustainable growth as an intangible cultural resource for the city.

f4b4bb981e:a375269525e93876.title: La Poste - NFTimbre 5
f4b4bb981e:a375269525e93876.summary: Des NFTimbres pour La Poste ! Il s'agit d'une planche de timbres NFT, sur le thème du "Coq Français". C'est une interprétation à la fois symbolique et décalée du coq français, figure emblématique du patrimoine national.

f4b4bb981e:66898b66634115ec.summary: SendIt is an on-demand logistics platform built for SMEs, online sellers, and fast moving businesess aggregating world wide top couriers into one dashboard where you book, track, manage returns, and control every shipment in real time, without the chaos.

a4977d3fa4:7803e1a8625f586c.title: Kylie Jenner Makes Victoria's Secret Runway Debut in $50 Million USD Diamond-Encrusted Jacob & Co. Fantasy Bra
a4977d3fa4:7803e1a8625f586c.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:7803e1a8625f586c.summary: Summary Kylie Jenner made her Victoria’s Secret runway debut at the 2026 Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show wearing the iconic Fantasy BraValued at $50 million USD the one-of-a-kind Jacob & Co. creation is the most expensive Fantasy Bra in the brand’s historyCrafted with 4,410 natural diamonds and a 75.54-carat yellow diamond centerpiece the design marks the return of the runway tradition for the first time since 2018 Kylie Jenner made her surprise runway debut at the 2026 Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show wearing the label's revived Fantasy Bra, a $50 million USD high-jewelry creation engineered in collaboration with Jacob & Co. The appearance marked the KHY founder’s first time ever walking a Victoria’s Secret catwalk.Designed by Jacob Arabo, the showpiece drew inspiration from Jacob & Co.’s Rare Touch Jewelry Collection and reimagined the traditional lingerie staple without using any fabric. Handcrafted by 15 artisans over more than 1,000 hours, the structure incorporates 3,218 individually designed components engineered to move with the body like lingerie. At the center sits a 75.54-carat natural Fancy Vivid Yellow diamond, encircled by 4,409 natural diamonds totaling 1,373 carats in an array of cuts, including the jeweler's signature Angel-Cut. Made entirely of precious metals and stones, covered in shimmering crystals, and finished with delicate fringe along the base, the $50 million USD piece stands as the most valuable Fantasy Bra ever produced.Jenner paired the diamond-encrusted top with a low-slung silver thong, an iridescent white miniskirt, clear PVC heels, and large feathery white wings as partner Timothée Chalamet and mother Kris Jenner cheered from the audience. The runway appearance brought the Fantasy Bra back to the stage for the first time since Elsa Hosk wore it in 2018, following historic iterations previously donned by Claudia Schiffer in 1996, Alessandra Ambrosio, and Adriana Lima. a4977d3fa4:1a8ae5d7f75f8001.title: Apple's iPhone Duo Reportedly Sells Out Moments After Pre-Orders Open
a4977d3fa4:1a8ae5d7f75f8001.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:1a8ae5d7f75f8001.summary: Summary Apple’s all-new iPhone Duo entered backorder status minutes after pre-orders went liveDelivery estimates across all configurations quickly slipped to mid and late November due to tight initial supply and high demandIn-store retail availability and initial customer shipments officially begin on October 23 Apple has seen its newly announced iPhone Duo rapidly sell out across digital storefronts, with delivery windows slipping moments after pre-orders opened at 8 a.m. ET. According to Apple Insider, the initial supply of the new hardware was quickly depleted across all configurations.Within minutes of launch, shipping windows for the device slipped back to November 16 and subsequently to November 23. While Apple traditionally maintains secrecy regarding exact launch inventory numbers, the extended dispatch times point to both significant early buyer demand and constrained launch-day volume. Reports highlight that the phone's intricate design has introduced complex manufacturing hurdles, limiting the initial production yield compared to conventional releases.Arriving as the most expensive iPhone model Apple has ever produced, the launch comes against the backdrop of an ongoing global chip shortage that has pushed electronics costs upward across the tech landscape. While customers can still submit backorders through online channels, supply for day-one fulfillment remains tightly restricted.The Apple iPhone Duo officially arrives in retail stores and begins initial customer deliveries on October 23, 2026. a4977d3fa4:a344c744230bddf1.title: Philadelphia 76ers Convert Tacko Fall to Two-Way Contract
a4977d3fa4:a344c744230bddf1.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:a344c744230bddf1.summary: Summary The Philadelphia 76ers have officially converted center Tacko Fall to a two-way contract ahead of the regular seasonThe roster move follows key frontcourt injuries including a season-ending Achilles tear for backup center Ariel HukportiFall enters his fourth NBA season after previously competing overseas for the Ningbo Rockets The Philadelphia 76ers have officially signed 7-foot-6 center Tacko Fall to a two-way contract, addressing frontcourt depth following multiple injuries during the preseason. The franchise announced the roster move on Saturday.Fall initially signed an Exhibit 10 deal with Philadelphia last month before earning an elevated roster designation. The frontcourt opening emerged after projected backup center Ariel Hukporti sustained a season-ending right Achilles tear during preseason play. Depth concerns compounded further with center Adem Bona sidelined by a foot ailment and Dominick Barlow missing the entire preseason slate due to persistent back soreness.The transaction marks Fall's return to the NBA for his fourth career campaign and his first appearance since the 2021-22 season with the Cleveland Cavaliers. The 30-year-old big man spent his initial two seasons with the Boston Celtics alongside current Sixers forward Jaylen Brown, before most recently playing in the Chinese Basketball Association with the Ningbo Rockets.Fall joins the 76ers' active rotation as the team works to stabilize its frontcourt rotation heading into the regular season. a4977d3fa4:5909e52f069bc83a.title: D'Angelo's Brother Confirms More Details of Posthumous Album Currently in Development
a4977d3fa4:5909e52f069bc83a.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:5909e52f069bc83a.summary: Summary Luther Archer has confirmed that a posthumous D'Angelo album is underway with six tracks already completedThe late singer's family is reviewing a vault of unreleased recordings that includes collaborations with Michael Jackson and Mary J. BligeThe project will mark the neo-soul pioneer's first full-length offering since 2014's 'Black Messiah' The estate of D'Angelo has confirmed that a posthumous album is officially in the works, drawing from an extensive personal vault of unreleased music. Following an interview with Kiss Richmond, the announcement arrives one year after the neo-soul pioneer passed away from pancreatic cancer in October 2025.Speaking on the upcoming material, the singer's older brother Luther Archer revealed that work has already commenced on the initial tracklist. “We've got an album coming out,” Archer stated. “There are six tracks [so far]. But then we have a whole vault of music that's never been released.” Archer explained that the estate is exploring several long-term releases, including a potential collection of b-sides, adding that “there's several projects down the road.” Among the archived recordings currently under consideration are unreleased collaborations featuring Mary J. Blige and Michael Jackson.The confirmation follows remarks from Questlove at the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame in November 2025, where he teased that forthcoming music from the vault represented “the sound of yesterday, but for the future.” Over his career, D’Angelo released only three studio albums—1995’s Brown Sugar, 2000’s Voodoo, and 2014’s Black Messiah—earning critical acclaim and two Grammy Awards for Best R&B Album. The newly announced project marks his first full-length effort in more than a decade. Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

a4977d3fa4:8b032a97bbca48b8.title: Sacramento Kings Guard Ben Simmons Sustains Season-Ending Torn Achilles Tendon
a4977d3fa4:8b032a97bbca48b8.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:8b032a97bbca48b8.summary: Summary Sacramento Kings guard Ben Simmons sustained a torn right Achilles tendon during Sunday’s practice and will undergo surgeryThe injury likely ends the three-time All-Star’s season following a strong training camp and preseason returnSimmons addressed the setback directly in a personal statement emphasizing resilience through adversity The Sacramento Kings have confirmed that guard Ben Simmons has sustained a torn right Achilles tendon and will undergo surgery, bringing an abrupt end to his anticipated return. The injury occurred during a live scrimmage drill at Sunday's team practice ahead of the upcoming NBA regular season.The 30-year-old veteran had recently completed an impressive training camp after rehabilitating from previous back surgeries, having signed a one-year, $3.5 million USD contract with Sacramento on September 4. Impressing general manager Scott Perry and head coach Doug Christie during workouts, Simmons was slated to serve as a versatile reclamation playmaker capable of defending across positions 1 through 5 while backing up rookie point guard Darius Acuff Jr. Over two preseason appearances for the Kings, Simmons averaged 10.5 points in 17.5 minutes of action.Simmons addressed the setback directly in a statement shared across his social media channels, "I've faced challenges before that tested me mentally, physically and emotionally, and I've found a way through every single one of them," Simmons wrote. "This injury is another chapter in my journey, not the end of my story.""It's never easy being away from the game I love, especially after everything it took to get back here," he continued. "But if there’s one thing I've learned, it's that adversity doesn't define you. How you respond to it does." Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

a4977d3fa4:d84bb27552fcccba.title: 'Street Fighter' Claims the Box Office Crown With a $31 Million USD Debut
a4977d3fa4:d84bb27552fcccba.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:d84bb27552fcccba.summary: Summary Paramount and Legendary’s video game adaptation 'Street Fighter' topped the domestic box office with a $31 million USD launch and $51.1 million USD globallyA24’s Elizabeth Holmes documentary 'You Can See Everything' exceeded tracking with a massive $15 million USD opening from just 855 theatersThe weekend also saw Netflix report theatrical box office grosses for the first time with specialty release La Bola Negra Paramount Pictures and Legendary Entertainment's live-action adaptation of Street Fighter has claimed the number one spot at the domestic box office, delivering a strong $31 million USD opening weekend. First reported by Rebecca Rubin, the video game adaptation led the charts ahead of a historic specialty debut from A24 and directing duo Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim for the documentary You Can See Everything.Directed by Kitao Sakurai and starring Noah Centineo and Andrew Koji, the $82 million USD Street Fighter production generated its chart-topping domestic haul across 3,575 venues, adding $20.1 million USD internationally for a $51.1 million USD worldwide bow. The project, co-financed by Legendary and Capcom, serves as the franchise's third live-action film following releases in 1994 and 2009.Securing second place, You Can See Everything stunned with a $15 million USD opening from just 855 screens. Produced in secret for approximately $7 million USD, the film marks the biggest opening weekend for a documentary in over two decades since 2004’s Fahrenheit 9/11, and the largest debut for any release playing in under 1,000 theaters since 2006’s Borat. Running nearly three hours, the documentary offers a candid look at Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes right before she began her 11-year prison sentence.Further down the chart, Universal’s Other Mommy secured third with $8.3 million USD, Disney’s Whalefall collected $8 million USD, and Focus Features’ Sense and Sensibility earned $7.2 million USD. a4977d3fa4:419821ffdf799f60.title: Carhartt WIP Reunited With Nike Sportswear and SUPPLY for SURPLUS 2026 Collection
a4977d3fa4:419821ffdf799f60.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:419821ffdf799f60.summary: Summary Carhartt WIP partnered with Nike Sportswear and SUPPLY to launch a limited collection for the SURPLUS festival in SydneyThe capsule was headlined by a souvenir Santa Fe Jacket crafted from heavyweight Dearborn Canvas with faux-leather sleeves alongside French terry staplesAvailable strictly in person the physical assortment dropped on October 17 at the SURPLUS Marketplace with no online release Carhartt WIP officially released its SURPLUS® 2026 collection, returning for its second year at the Sydney music and culture festival presented by Nike Sportswear and SUPPLY®. Conceived as an elevated take on festival merchandise, the commemorative capsule was sold strictly on site across the event weekend.Anchoring the release was a limited-edition souvenir Santa Fe Jacket, constructed with a signature heavyweight Dearborn Canvas body and collar, contrasting faux-leather sleeves, and a quilted nylon lining. Custom co-branded Carhartt WIP, Nike Sportswear, and SURPLUS® embroidery detailed the outerwear piece throughout. Alongside the jacket, the lineup delivered a Zip Hooded Sweater and matching Fleece Shorts tailored from cotton French terry, supported by short- and long-sleeve T-shirts crafted from 100% cotton.The visual palette drew directly from the core signature hues of each collaborator: Carhartt WIP’s trademark Hamilton Brown, Nike Sportswear’s vibrant orange, and SURPLUS®’s SUPPLY® Blue. An overarching Urban Camo pattern unified the range, nodding to the spirit of exploration across the festival's Darlinghurst precinct. In tandem with the apparel release, Carhartt WIP hosted an evening showcase on October 16 at Oxford Art Factory, featuring a live performance by electronic trio Suzy Sheer.The Carhartt WIP x Nike Sportswear x SURPLUS® collection released exclusively on site at the SURPLUS® Marketplace on Saturday, October 17, 2026 onwards. a4977d3fa4:8884d438f72d1dc7.title: Bartosz Sztybor Warns Fans Not To Get Too Attached to ‘Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2'

a4977d3fa4:8884d438f72d1dc7.summary: Night City has always been the real antagonist of the Cyberpunk universe — a sprawling, neon-drenched meat grinder where people don't so much survive as try to go down in flames on their own terms. That bleak philosophy gave the original Cyberpunk: Edgerunners much of its emotional punch, turning a standalone anime into a gateway to the wider Cyberpunk universe while helping to revitalize interest in the game franchise.But part of what made the anime resonate so deeply with audiences was precisely that David and Lucy's story had reached a definitive conclusion. In today's entertainment landscape, where successful franchises are rarely allowed to end on their own terms, that sense of finality was arguably one of Edgerunners' greatest strengths. Naturally, when Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2 was announced, it raised a rather obvious question: what exactly was left to continue?As it turns out, showrunner Bartosz Sztybor had already been developing ideas for future Edgerunners stories while writing the original series. Conversations with Studio TRIGGER about the franchise's future were also underway before its 2022 premiere. The distinction, however, was never about revisiting David and Lucy's story, but rather exploring the countless other lives unfolding across Night City.Scheduled to premiere on Netflix on October 20, the new ten-episode series introduces an entirely different ensemble, with Kai Ikarashi taking over directorial duties from Hiroyuki Imaishi. But beyond its new characters and creative direction, Edgerunners 2 also raises bigger questions about how CD Projekt Red intends to develop the wider Cyberpunk universe.Just days ahead of the premiere, Hypebeast jumped on a Zoom call with Sztybor to unpack the sequel's secret origins, Studio TRIGGER's changing of the guard, and why viewers should never get too attached to anyone in Night City.When the first Edgerunners aired, CD Projekt Red made it quite clear that it was intended as a standalone story. a4977d3fa4:902f255d0fd40436.title: Vacheron Constantin’s First Concours d’Élégance Spotlights 34 Historic Watches
a4977d3fa4:902f255d0fd40436.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:902f255d0fd40436.summary: Summary Phillips and Vacheron Constantin announced 34 finalists for the inaugural Concours d’Elégance Horlogère.A 14-member jury evaluated over 550 vintage timepieces spanning 1755 to 1999.Winners will be revealed in Geneva on November 10 following a public exhibition. Organized as an initiative by Phillips in Association with Bacs & Russo, Vacheron Constantin has officially announced the finalists for its inaugural Concours d’Elégance Horlogère. Billed as the first-ever "Concours d'Élégance" dedicated exclusively to haute horlogerie, this landmark event pays tribute to the international community of watch collectors and the Swiss manufacturer's 271-year heritage.The competition invites enthusiasts from around the globe to showcase their historically significant Vacheron Constantin timepieces, celebrating the pure, timeless beauty and enduring legacy of watches that have been cherished and passed down through generations. More than 550 owner-submitted timepieces were entered following the competition’s announcement earlier this year, spanning pocket watches and wristwatches made by Vacheron Constantin between 1755 and 1999. After authentication and evaluation by the Maison’s master watchmakers and Heritage experts, 95 pieces advanced to jury review before being narrowed to 34 finalists.The competition is divided across seven categories - Chronographs, Métiers d’Art, Chronomètre Royal, Astronomical Complications, Multiple Complications, Design and Chiming Mechanisms - creating a cross-section of more than two centuries of Vacheron Constantin watchmaking. Among the finalists are exceptionally rare and, in some cases, unique pieces: a steel Reference 4072 chronograph from 1940; a 1957 rectangular platinum full-calendar and moon-phase watch produced as a single piece; a one-off 1940 “Don Pancho” minute repeater with retrograde full date; and ornate cloisonné enamel watches depicting maps of the Americas and Europe. The selection also stretches into later neo-vintage…

a4977d3fa4:0e9092223a79d7e4.title: Quentin Tarantino Confirms Finishing Script for 10th Film but Delays Production to "Live a Little"
a4977d3fa4:0e9092223a79d7e4.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:0e9092223a79d7e4.summary: Summary Quentin Tarantino has completed writing the script for his tenth and final feature filmThe filmmaker is delaying production to focus on his London stage play 'The Popinjay Cavalier' and spend time with familyThe swashbuckling comedy starring Sacha Baron Cohen opens at the Phoenix Theatre next March and runs through June 13 Quentin Tarantino has completed the script for his 10th feature film, though the director plans to hold off on production until his London stage production finishes its run. The filmmaker shared the update during an appearance on The Graham Norton Show, marking his first visit to the program in over a decade.Tarantino reaffirmed his longstanding plan to retire from filmmaking after ten features, but made it clear that he will not rush into production. "I've written a script that I really like, but I want to do the play and see who I am; then I'll then go back and spend time with my family and live a little and then see what I want to do,” Tarantino said.His immediate creative focus is centered on The Popinjay Cavalier, which originated as a screenplay before transitioning into a stage production. “It really worked as a play,” Tarantino explained, adding, “I think it will be thrilling.” Billed as a swashbuckling comedy starring Sacha Baron Cohen, the production marks the filmmaker’s West End debut following his 2019 Oscar-winning film Once Upon a Time in Hollywood. “I’m keen with anticipation to give the West End a great night out,” Tarantino noted.The Popinjay Cavalier begins previews in late February before officially opening at London’s Phoenix Theatre next March, running through June 13. Set against jazz and rap-inflected sequences, the trailer introduces several figures who will shape Makoto’s early life while charting the circumstances that begin pushing him toward a career as a showman.The Kokura trailer is the first in a planned series of story previews following Makoto across Stranger Than Heaven’s five eras and cities, spanning 1915 to 1965. RGG Studio’s latest action-adventure moves from Kokura to Kure in 1929, Minami in 1943, Atami in 1951 and eventually Kamurocho in 1965, using each period to trace the protagonist’s changing identity against a reimagined half-century of Japanese history.First introduced as Project Century before receiving its official title, the game combines the studio’s character-driven storytelling and close-quarters combat with show-business elements, with Orpheus’ early influence appearing to establish music and performance as an important part of Makoto’s development.…

a4977d3fa4:39d6172a29f6c4fd.title: ‘Bleach: Thousand-Year Blood War – The Calamity’ Drops Its Final Trailer
a4977d3fa4:39d6172a29f6c4fd.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:39d6172a29f6c4fd.summary: Summary Bleach: Thousand-Year Blood War - The Calamity releases its final promotional trailer.The preview centers on Ichigo’s climactic confrontation with Yhwach.The final two episodes arrive October 19 and October 26, 2026. Bleach: Thousand-Year Blood War - The Calamity has released its final promotional trailer ahead of the anime’s last two episodes, bringing Ichigo Kurosaki’s confrontation with Yhwach into its closing stretch.Titled “THE LAST PV,” the video opens by condensing the major battles and turning points that have carried the Thousand-Year Blood War arc toward its climax, before shifting into new footage from the finale. Ichigo and Yhwach remain at the center of the preview as the Quincy King’s plan threatens all three worlds, while Uryu Ishida, the remaining Soul Reapers and their unlikely allies are shown converging on the final conflict. The trailer leans heavily into the scale of the endgame, moving between fractured landscapes, rapid combat sequences and the mounting destruction surrounding Yhwach’s attempt to reshape reality.The Calamity serves as the fourth and final cour of the Thousand-Year Blood War adaptation, which began in 2022 and brought Tite Kubo’s concluding manga arc to animation more than a decade after the original Bleach television series ended. Produced by PIERROT FILMS, the final installment premiered in July 2026 under chief series director Tomohisa Taguchi and series director Hikaru Murata, with Kubo continuing to supervise the adaptation. Episodes 49 and 50 were previously delayed to allow additional production time as the series approached its climax; the penultimate episode will now stream on October 19, followed by the series finale on October 26. In the U.S., both subtitled episodes will arrive on Hulu, while Disney+ will carry the conclusion internationally. Read more at Hypebeast

a4977d3fa4:d05b2a33fc202c53.summary: Summary ringles has introduced its Once You Drop Halloween sweepstakes offering a custom precious metal urn and 200 years of free chipsThe activation draws inspiration from can inventor Fredric Baur whose ashes were buried inside one of his packaging designs in 2008Participants can enter by signing a digital will and taste-ament through October 22 with one winner chosen around October 31 Pringles has officially launched the Pringles "Once You Drop" Campaign, challenging die-hard snackers to trade their final resting place for a 200-year supply of chips. Reviving that macabre legacy, the sweepstakes features a one-of-a-kind urn forged from precious metal, complete with a removable lid, personalized engraving, and the signature dimensions of the original canister.Alongside the bespoke container, the winner receives what the brand terms an “afterlifetime” supply of chips spanning two centuries, which can be legally bequeathed to future heirs. “Pringles has always been about the joy of the unexpected and this campaign takes our ‘Once You Drop’ campaign tagline literally: the pop don’t stop, not even once fans ‘drop,’” said Mauricio Jenkins, Salty Snacks Brand & Content Lead at Mars Snacking North America. a4977d3fa4:bbda12717d4cc9f3.title: Why Denis Villeneuve Needed James Bond to Finally Leave 'Dune' Behind
a4977d3fa4:bbda12717d4cc9f3.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:bbda12717d4cc9f3.summary: Summary Denis Villeneuve revealed that signing on to direct the next James Bond film gave him the momentum needed to conclude his 'Dune' trilogyAdapting Frank Herbert’s Dune Messiah the third chapter picks up 17 years later as Paul Atreides succumbs to tyrannical powerWarner Bros will release Dune Part Three in theaters on December 18 2026 Warner Bros. and director Denis Villeneuve have shared fresh insight into Dune: Part Three, with the filmmaker revealing how the upcoming James Bond installment serves as his creative escape from the sci-fi franchise. In an interview with Empire, the director reflected candidly on avoiding complacency for the final chapter.Explaining his decision to return to Arrakis, Villeneuve noted that his motivation stemmed from fatigue rather than fond memories. "Maybe it's a good idea to go back to this project, not out of nostalgia, not because I miss it, but the opposite — I'm tired of it," Villeneuve explained. "I want to make sure that I will be severe with the material. That I will not be complacent. I thought, 'When it's done, I need a very powerful rocket to pull me away from Arrakis.' When I was asked to do the next Bond, I said: 'OK, this is what I need.'"Adapting Frank Herbert’s Dune Messiah, the concluding installment jumps 17 years into the future to chronicle Paul Atreides’ (Timothée Chalamet) descent into tyrannical rule. "The idea was to try to make a movie that will have the same DNA — it’s a Dune movie — but it's a very different movie," Villeneuve said. "It has a different pacing. We are back with the same characters, but this time the world has totally changed. Their psyches, their perspective on reality has totally changed, and Paul is living with the burden of what he created, trying to find a way out of this spiral of violence."Dune: Part Three hits theaters on December 18, 2026. What started as a bizarre inconvenience soon became the unlikely foundation for his third studio album, MOSCA.At the time, NSQK was reading Franz Kafka’s The Metamorphosis, a story that began to feel strangely connected to his own life. Between the unexplained infestation, a spiritual cleansing, and the growing pressures of the Latin music industry, he questioned how success seemed to transform him. The flies became a symbol of everything that comes with chasing greatness: envy, ego, criticism, competition, and the constant hunger for more.That tension runs throughout MOSCA. Bringing rock influences into his signature blend of electronic music, pop, and hip-hop, NSQK pushes his sound into new territory across 17 heavy-hitting tracks. Collaborations with Julieta Venegas, Jean Dawson, Eslabón Armado, Kevin Kaarl, and Riosse also mark a shift in his creative process, as he opens the door to more voices and perspectives.We caught up with NSQK to discuss the strange events that inspired MOSCA, the artistic evolution behind his most ambitious record yet, and his plans to bring an entirely new live experience to Mexico City's Estadio GNP Seguros in January 2027.What inspired the title of your new album, MOSCA?“In 2024, I moved into a small apartment in Monterrey with my girlfriend, who is now my wife. a4977d3fa4:9cb8cbbe0e92696a.title: ‘All About Alana’ Charts the Making of an NYC It Girl
a4977d3fa4:9cb8cbbe0e92696a.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:9cb8cbbe0e92696a.summary: Summary 'All About Alana,' a new group photo show curated by Ryan McGinley, has opened at Primary Photographic's Rectangle Room in NYCThe exhibition figures actress, model, and musician Alana Jessica Martin through the lens of 30+ notable downtown photographers, exploring the mythology of the muses throughout art history and the role they play in contemporary culture Dating almost as far back as art history is the artist’s muse. One of its more enduring forms in culture is the It Girl, the one who will never wear wrong, always influence, not be influenced. She might not be the first you notice when you walk in a room, but will be the only one you think of when you leave, mastering the kind of elusive cool that won’t ever budge. Every era of New York can be understood by its It’s, Grace Jones, Jenny Shimizu, or Chlöe Sevigny, among them. It's 2026, and a new star has risen.All eyes are on Alana Jessica Martin in a new photo show at Rectangle Room in New York. Curated by Ryan McGinley, All About Alana puts the actress, model, musician, and nightlife darling center stage, tracing the lure of the modern-day muse and her many mythologies.The exhibition features work by over 30 New York-based photographers, spanning selfies, Polaroids, photobooth strips, and gritty black-and-whites, each capturing Martin’s likeness in their own signature styles. One image, the wall-wide opener, channels the drama of a pop confessional, Martin laid bare, with a tear-stained stare locked on the lens; another, high-flashed, sees the artist coolly sipping on Pepsi at Katz’s. Some are explicit in their nod to the other reigning All-American bombshells, with a tattered stripes-and-stars flag high, while Martin stands knee-deep in waves.It’s also a who’s who of downtown photography, so study up, pulling an intergenerational lineup of some of the most exciting image-makers on the scene, such as Daniel Arnold, Charles Caesar, Quil Harwood-Lemons, Jonah Ali Hodari, Jae Kim, Clifford Prince King,…

a4977d3fa4:c1f58ab2a8502511.title: Lil Yachty’s Nike Tech Collection Is Larger Than Life
a4977d3fa4:c1f58ab2a8502511.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:c1f58ab2a8502511.summary: Summary Lil Yachty’s first Nike apparel collab drops today, with an oversized Tech Fleece zip-up hoodie and below-the-knee shorts, both in black and navy, with heavyweight double-layer construction and Yachty branding.The raffle is for the Lil Yachty x Nike Tech Collection is exclusively available on yachty.shop. Lil Yachty’s first Nike apparel collaboration lands today, October 16, with a reworked take on the iconic Tech Fleece. Dubbed the “best-dressed rappers on the scene” by the brand, the lineup pushes proportions to the extreme in Yachty-style elevated basics, oversized silhouettes, and techy details.The collection features a Tech Fleece zip-up hoodie and 3/4-length shorts, both in black and navy colorways. Both pieces use an oversized fit, double-layer heavyweight construction, and the signature Nike Tech chevron lines. The zip-up adds a structured balaclava hood, adjustable bungee cords, and thumbholes. The fleece shorts fall below the knee and feature cargo pockets, adjustable snaps, and bungee cords, all reimagined with updated neck-tag branding, snap pockets, and custom label graphics with Yachty’s touch.With the tagline “Not everybody fits in,” the campaign stars NBA player Bol Bol alongside Yachty, with teasers directed by the rapper and Cam Hicks. In one, Yachty towers over a crowd at a DMV in his blacked-out Tech Fleece. When asked to straighten up for his photo, he knocks his head through the ceiling, and drywall dust lands on his shoulders. In the campaign’s other teaser, Bol Bol squeezes into a crammed elevator and tries to get someone to press the button for his floor, but everyone is too distracted by his 7'3" stature. The raffle for Lil Yachty’s Nike Tech collaboration is exclusively on yachty.shop. Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

a4977d3fa4:e42b2574148d31bb.title: Pro Photographer Megan Collante's Latest Shoot Exemplifies Unbreakable Tradition
a4977d3fa4:e42b2574148d31bb.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:e42b2574148d31bb.summary: Toyota has tapped NYC-native photographer Megan Collante to present "A City in Frame: Some Things Never Change," featuring the bZ, part of Toyota’s New All-Electric Family.Since middle school, Kenny and Alex have had a ritual: after school, Alex would be waiting outside by the buses and the two would go get ice cream – no plan, no discussion needed. It's stuck around ever since, even as everything else about their lives changed.Kenny has finally put his brushes down after a 12-hour day in the studio, paint still under his fingernails. His art has only gotten bigger, messier, more demanding as his career has taken off – bigger canvases, later nights, more of himself poured into every piece. But no matter how complicated the day gets, the drive to their spot never does. Alex just puts the bZ in gear and goes, its electrifying performance makes the trip through Manhattan traffic feel effortless and exhilarating, like no time has passed since they were 12 years old. With the touch of a finger, the same playlist they’ve been curating since middle school plays on repeat, turning the bZ into a sanctuary of comfort. And when their one scoop turns into a long night of unwinding through the driving roads near Storm King Mountain, there’s no worry about getting home: miles of charge means a night of memory making.Their tradition bends, but it never breaks. In the end, some things never change.Check out Megan Collante's "A City in Frame: Some Things Never Change," and learn moreabout the all-electric bZ here.Disclaimer: All vehicles displayed are not in motion. a4977d3fa4:9b60105abd56ddcb.title: Ressence’s TYPE 10 DN Is Designed to Look Like One Continuous Object
a4977d3fa4:9b60105abd56ddcb.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:9b60105abd56ddcb.summary: Summary Ressence debuts the TYPE 10 DN, its first oil-filled watch powered by an in-house movement.The 41.5mm titanium watch uses a seamless deep-blue “Dark Night” treatment.Its ROCS 10 display and RW-04 calibre deliver dual-time functionality and 60 hours of reserve. Ressence is introducing the TYPE 10 DN (Dark Night), a 100-piece limited edition that represents one of the Antwerp independent’s most ambitious attempts to make mechanical complexity disappear from view.Four years in development, the TYPE 10 began as a series of sketches by founder Benoît Mintiens exploring how a watch might evolve if shaped by the same principles of efficiency, integration and fluidity found in nature. The result is Ressence’s first oil-filled watch powered by its own movement, with the case, dial and integrated rubber strap visually merging into a single deep-blue form. Its 41.5mm Grade 5 titanium case is polished and treated with hard DLC, while the oil-filled display optically pulls the dial toward the sapphire crystal, further dissolving the usual boundaries between case, crystal and time display.Beneath that streamlined exterior sits a remarkably elaborate system comprising 538 components. Ressence’s patented ROCS 10 display replaces conventional hands with rotating discs for the hours, minutes and second time zone, alongside a 120-second runner that also acts as a mechanical shock absorber and a color-coded oil-temperature indicator. Driving it is the newly developed RW-04 self-winding calibre, designed in-house for the TYPE 10 and delivering a 60-hour power reserve from twin barrels.Because the mechanical movement operates in air while the ROCS display moves through oil, the two are housed in separate hermetically sealed chambers and connected magnetically through a 0.1mm titanium membrane. The arrangement allows power to transfer without a physical shaft passing between the two environments, while an expansion chamber compensates for changes in oil volume as temperatures…

a4977d3fa4:5f2ae3813a2f7627.title: Bocci Reimagines Its 14 Series With a Liquid-Like Mirror Effect
a4977d3fa4:5f2ae3813a2f7627.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:5f2ae3813a2f7627.summary: Summary Bocci debuts the 14 Mirror lighting collection at Paris Art & Design Week.The hand-applied mirrored finish dynamically oscillates between transparency and reflection.Milanese duo Cameranesi Pompili introduced the series through a constellation-like installation. Bocci is expanding one of its best-known lighting families with 14 Mirror, a reflective new treatment for the Vancouver studio’s iconic 14 series. The new lighting fixtures are defined by an oscillating, perceptual relationship between light transmission and environmental reflection. When fully illuminated, the internal light passes straight through the glass, rendering the orb fully transparent.However, when switched off or dimmed, a mirror effect takes over, turning the ambient light of the room, sunlight, or even a window into an active part of the fixture's composition. Between these two extremes lies a dynamic gradient condition where the solid glass at once transmits its own glow while softly reflecting its surroundings, creating a fluid visual experience that never quite settles into a single, fixed image.The new finish is intentionally inconsistent, with subtle variations in opacity created through the hand-application process. Those differences allow each piece to respond uniquely to its environment, with reflections appearing to slide, soften and dissolve across the glass as viewing angles and ambient light change. Bocci co-founder Omer Arbel describes 14 Mirror less as a color than a “condition,” and that idea becomes especially clear in clustered compositions, where the pieces move between luminous glass objects and dark, liquid-like reflective spheres. The treatment will be offered across the existing 14 typologies, including the 14p portable, 14 pendant and 14s sconce, giving the established series a new visual language without abandoning its underlying construction.To introduce the collection, Bocci has partnered with Milan-based duo Cameranesi Pompili on ORBITAL, a scenographic…

a4977d3fa4:61e4c036adb2c503.title: Byredo and Iittala Turn Light and Scent Into Sculptural Objects
a4977d3fa4:61e4c036adb2c503.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:61e4c036adb2c503.summary: Summary Byredo and Iittala expand LJUS into a full glass home collection.Sculptural forms explore the interaction of light, scent and flame.Five handcrafted pieces launch globally on October 16, 2026. Following its initial reveal earlier this year, Byredo and Iittala are bringing their LJUS collaboration into full view, expanding the project into a complete collection of glass objects built around the relationship between light, scent and everyday ritual.Rooted in a shared Nordic design sensibility, the partnership combines Iittala’s glassmaking heritage with Byredo’s more atmospheric approach to fragrance, treating flame not simply as a functional element but as something that activates the objects themselves. The collection takes inspiration from the changing character of Nordic light, balancing ideas of fire and ice, permanence and ephemerality through sculptural forms intended to subtly alter the mood of a room.The lineup comprises a candle stand, candle ornament, light refractor, incense holder and fragrance diffuser vessel, each handcrafted at Iittala’s historic factory in Finland. Visually, the pieces share a pronounced rippled and faceted glass language, with thick transparent walls catching and distorting surrounding light while amplifying the movement of a flame within. The light refractor is the most architectural expression of that idea, wrapping a candle within a substantial undulating glass shell, while the diffuser vessel translates the same silhouette into a smaller form with a softly tinted lower section. a4977d3fa4:becc7bb3bd288bb8.summary: Summary Tesla has unveiled a flying second-generation Roadster concept engineered in partnership with SpaceXArmed with rechargeable compressed-air thrusters and underside suction fans the electric coupe claims a 0 to 60 mph sprint in 0.81 secondsProduction for the aerospace-inspired two-seater is slated to begin in 2028 Tesla has officially showcased its flying second-generation Roadster, demonstrating extreme airborne capabilities powered by rocket propulsion systems developed in collaboration with SpaceX. The concept test run saw the electric coupe clear rows of parked vehicles, launch off half-pipe ramps, and maneuver completely upside down.Engineered in tandem with SpaceX, the high-performance two-seater incorporates a network of compressed-air thrusters into its underbody and rear to generate lift, stabilize stationary hops, and cushion landings. Powered by fuel-free, rechargeable onboard air tanks, the rear-facing thrusters double as launch boosters, rocketing the vehicle from 0 to 60 mph in a claimed 0.81 seconds. To tackle inverted driving on vertical half-pipes, the chassis utilizes an integrated fan suction system to maintain continuous downward grip.Tesla chief designer Franz von Holzhausen penned the exterior with an "aerospace aesthetic," outfitting the hard-top coupe with angular bodywork, scissor doors, and an active deployable spoiler. Inside, the vehicle features seats molded directly to the structural chassis and an electronic steer-by-wire system that eliminates mechanical steering linkages. While Elon Musk noted that street legality remains unconfirmed, the production version is intended to serve as the only driver-operated vehicle in Tesla's future lineup.Production on the Tesla Roadster is scheduled to begin in 2028.Real life, baby https://t.co/3QEqn18wig— Tesla (@Tesla) October 16, 2026Do a kickflip! https://t.co/DJ1Bq1yu8m— Tesla (@Tesla) October 16, 2026 Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

a4977d3fa4:f27128da9825a90a.title: A Brutal Crime in Golden Gate Park Unravels a Household in Official 'Josephine' Trailer
a4977d3fa4:f27128da9825a90a.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:f27128da9825a90a.summary: Summary Sumerian Pictures has released the official trailer for the double Sundance award-winning drama 'Josephine'Directed by Beth de Araújo the film stars Channing Tatum Gemma Chan and newcomer Mason Reeves navigating the aftermath of a violent crimeThe drama opens in select theaters on November 20 before rolling out nationwide on December 4 Sumerian Pictures has officially released the first trailer for Josephine, the acclaimed drama from writer-director Beth de Araújo (Soft & Quiet). The film earned both the U.S. Dramatic Grand Jury Prize and the Audience Award at the Sundance Film Festival.Drawing from de Araújo’s childhood experience witnessing a violent crime alongside her father in San Francisco’s Golden Gate Park, the project explores the lingering silence and psychological fallout of unresolved trauma. Newcomer Mason Reeves stars as eight-year-old Josephine, whose frightening encounter leaves her increasingly fearful and prone to acting out, while Channing Tatum and Gemma Chan portray parents clashing over how to guide their daughter while coping with their own vulnerability.The film’s official synopsis reads, "Josephine follows the psychological fallout after eight-year-old Josephine (Reeves) witnesses a brutal crime in Golden Gate Park. As she acts out, her parents (Tatum and Chan) struggle with helping their daughter cope, while facing the moral responsibility of demanding justice in a world that’s lost its innocence."Rounding out the cast are Philip Ettinger, Syra McCarthy, and Eleanore Pienta. Produced by David Kaplan, Josh Peters, de Araújo, Marina Stabile, Tatum, Chan, Mark H. Rapaport, Josh Beirne-Golden, and Crystine Zhang, the film balances intimate domestic turmoil with the weight of seeking justice.Josephine arrives in select theaters on November 20 before expanding nationwide on December 4. a4977d3fa4:16df8e66ca7d396a.title: COMME des GARÇONS Revives Its Cult Magazine, ‘Six’
a4977d3fa4:16df8e66ca7d396a.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:16df8e66ca7d396a.summary: Summary Rei Kawakubo's COMME des GARÇONS magazine, 'Six,' is brought back in print as an exclusive mailer, featuring archival covers and images, paired with new works that embody its spiritThe revival also takes shape as a series of installations in at COMME des GARÇONS Aoyama, and Dover Street Market's Paris and London locations, wrapping architecture in blown-up images from archival issuesA limited-edition collection of 12 tees, each emblazoned with art from the magazine, is also available online and in-person at DSM COMME des GARÇONS’ Six is back. The cult magazine by Rei Kawakubo sees a revival this Frieze with installations in London, Paris, and Tokyo, a tee collection, and, true to form, a print edition.First published in 1988, Six ran for just eight editions before ending in 1991, but its imprint on fashion, art, and image culture, remain as relevant as ever. A conceptual look book for the brand, the biannual offered a post-clothing vision of fashion that pushed past the industry and into realms of design, film, architecture, art and photography. Salvador Dalí, Robert Frank, Jean-Paul Gaultier, Peter Lindbergh, Issey Miyake, and Yohji Yamamoto were among the contributors.“High fashion has to have a mystery about it,” Kawakubo once said. “This is the next step: visual representation of the collection, purely for image.” Only a few of its pages actually featured COMME des GARÇONS clothing.The first in 35 years, the new issue brings together six archival covers and various pages, paired with works from today’s image-makers that embeody the spirit of Six, curated by Kawakubo herself. According to Adrian Joffe, the president of Comme des Garçons International, the magazines were shared to select clients in the installations’ cities as mailers. It’s to be expected given the label’s rep for avant-garde, discreet branding. d006da4fe3:22627d45ff3f3498.author: Michael Albertus
d006da4fe3:22627d45ff3f3498.summary: Over the last half millennium, societies around the globe competed to divide up the world’s land. Nearly every square inch of soil outside Antarctica is now owned and tucked within national borders. But the oceans have largely been spared that fate. There were times throughout history when countries tried to gate and regulate the seas, but they were too vast to be controlled for long periods. During the Cold War, as technology made it far easier to imagine partitioning the world’s waterways and seabeds, great powers avoided an unrestrained race to grab the oceans. Most governments agreed to deal with them through a patchwork of treaties and multilateral bodies that sought to guarantee freedom of navigation in international waters and assign coastal seabeds to adjacent littoral states.

d006da4fe3:a574167532370f34.title: The Trouble With the Nuclear-AI Analogy
d006da4fe3:a574167532370f34.author: Christopher LaRoche, Ankit Panda
d006da4fe3:a574167532370f34.summary: In humanity’s quest to constrain the dangers from fast-advancing artificial intelligence, many have looked to the most revolutionary technology that preceded it: nuclear weapons. SpaceX CEO Elon Musk has called artificial intelligence “far more dangerous than nukes.” Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, who assigns The Making of the Atomic Bomb to employees and has likened himself to the Manhattan Project scientist Leo Szilard, describes the most powerful AI models as “weaponizable nuclear materials.” When asked how a technology such as AI can be regulated, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman often references the world’s nuclear materials watchdog, the International Atomic Energy Agency. Even the director of the CIA, John Ratcliffe, has made the same comparison.These comparisons capture real parallels. Like nuclear weapons, frontier AI is powerful and hard to control. Like nuclear technology, it can be used for good or for ill. And like the Cold War arms race, the race for AI breakthroughs may reorder the global balance of power. The nuclear analogy, then, seems to offer a blueprint for how to effectively govern a promising but potentially dangerous technology such as AI.

fc066e842d:ad406854d994c755.title: Ideas and Firm Dynamics When It Takes Two to Tango
fc066e842d:ad406854d994c755.author: Honghao Wang
fc066e842d:ad406854d994c755.summary: Teams of inventors now produce over 80 percent of U.S. patents, up from just 45 percent in 1976. Over the same period, inventor employment has become increasingly concentrated in large firms, rising six times more than overall employment concentration. To explain these trends, we develop a new model of endogenous team formation within firms and embed it in a general equilibrium model of the inventor labor market. Teams increase firms’ returns to scale by increasing the likelihood of productive matches between inventors. The value of these matches rises over time, possibly driven by increasing knowledge specialization. This causes large firms to expand and small firms to shrink in equilibrium, accounting for the observed increase in inventor employment concentration. Because firms do not internalize knowledge spillovers, there is misallocation of inventors across firms. The rise of team production amplifies this misallocation by a factor of six by reallocating inventors away from small firms that generate disproportionately large knowledge spillovers.

fc066e842d:49934de94c848c00.title: Relative Development and the Intelligence Divide: Human Capital, Technology Diffusion, and AI
fc066e842d:49934de94c848c00.author: Jonathan R. W. Temple
fc066e842d:49934de94c848c00.summary: Will artificial intelligence (AI) help poorer countries catch up? This paper argues that the answer depends less on access to AI than on the capacity to use new knowledge productively. We show that countries have narrowed gaps in capital and schooling more readily than gaps in productivity. Technology can diffuse widely without producing productivity convergence. Measured human capital explains only a modest share of productivity differences in levels, but is associated with sharply different mobility regimes. The estimated transition processes imply an expected time to exit the lowest-productivity state of about 65 years for economies below the estimated human-capital threshold, compared with about 25 years for those above it. This reconciles development accounting with the view of human capital as absorptive capacity. If AI mainly augments skilled workers and capable firms, it may reinforce existing gaps. If it lowers the costs of learning, adaptation, and implementation in weaker-capability economies, it could instead promote convergence. The Intelligence Divide is therefore not simply about access to AI, but about the capacity to turn knowledge into productivity.

fc066e842d:e0411ad22edea77d.title: Growth in Chains: EU Value Chain Productivity and its Slowdown
fc066e842d:e0411ad22edea77d.author: Lähdemäki, Sakari
fc066e842d:e0411ad22edea77d.summary: Abstract We study Europe’s post-2008 productivity slowdown using novel total factor productivity (TFP) measures that follow production beyond individual industries in global value chains (GVCs). We collect a newset of stylized facts: (1) the slowdown is broad-based, with productivity growth weakening both in final-producer industries and in upstream industries; (2) the staggered entry into force of bilateral investment treaties with China is followed by higher value-chain TFP and greater business-intangible investment; while (3) the gains associated with technology intangibles are weak. We use these facts to discipline a stylized two-region general-equilibrium model with business capabilities, technology-related knowledge, and cross-border knowledge spillovers. The calibration supports a two-stage interpretation of Europe’s experience: (1) sizeable initial integration gains because accumulated business capabilities convert market access into productivity, and (2) later losses when technology improvements are converted into productivity more effectively elsewhere.

fc066e842d:1aed792933eb29e0.title: A Fork in the Road for Global AI Governance: To Repair or Reconfigure Expert-Led Governance?
fc066e842d:1aed792933eb29e0.author: Olugbade, Olajide
fc066e842d:1aed792933eb29e0.summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) has become a live object of global governance, with expert-led institutional arrangements emerging across an international regime complex. While scholarship on epistemic communities and science-policy interfaces treats expertise as a mechanism for coordination under uncertainty, recent work in Objectual International Relations (O-IR) and Science and Technology Studies foregrounds knowledge politics, contested authority, and the co-productive character of governance. We bring these perspectives into conversation with AI governance through a reflexive workshop design using Nominal Group Technique, drawing on two expert workshops in the UK and US. Findings show that expert panels remain valued for structuring debate, coordinating knowledge, and lending legitimacy to policy action. Yet participants identified tensions around exclusion, elite and private capture, weak accountability, geopolitical constraints, and temporal misalignment between institutional processes and technological change. An object-centered analysis further shows that AI remains an unstable governance object; the knowledge required to govern it is contested and unevenly distributed; and expertise itself is politically charged and institutionally unsettled. We synthesize these tensions into two pathways: Repair and Reconfiguration. Repair seeks to stabilize AI as a governable object, standardize relevant knowledge, and secure expert authority through institutional continuity and procedural refinement. Reconfiguration seeks to keep AI contested, broaden credible forms of knowledge, and reshape expertise through participation, reflexivity, and engagement with politics. The framework provides a critical lens for assessing emerging institutional designs for global AI governance and the trade-offs they entail.

fc066e842d:cd03bbb2b7c0e7e7.title: From Individual to Social Imitation: How Communities Expand Organizational Search
fc066e842d:cd03bbb2b7c0e7e7.author: Christopher Tucci
fc066e842d:cd03bbb2b7c0e7e7.summary: Generative artificial intelligence illustrates a broader organizational puzzle: young, resource-constrained firms can build on knowledge produced across a wider field to address problems that exceed their internal experience. We theorize one mechanism as social imitation: a distributed and recursive process through which communities observe practices and outcomes across organizations, distill recurrent elements into portable strategies, circulate them, and revise the collective repertoire as adoption produces new evidence. This perspective endogenizes the object of imitation. Organizations do not merely copy practices; communities collectively produce what becomes available to copy. We distinguish the source of a candidate (directly observed organizations or a collective) from its mode of adoption (blind or informed), and examine four forms of imitation in an agent-based model of organizational search. Collective sourcing alone does not improve performance. Its value depends on situated evaluation: assessing whether a candidate fits the adopter's configuration. As interdependence increases, informed social imitation improves population performance and the best solution discovered. As problems grow, it becomes more likely to outperform informed imitation from one or several directly observed peers because collective distillation sustains a broader candidate repertoire. Most gains arise from evaluating a small candidate set, and population performance can improve when only a minority of organizations possesses evaluative capability. Social imitation thus reveals a division of cognitive labor: communities expand the strategies organizations can consider, while organizations create value by determining which strategies fit. It explains how firms can mobilize knowledge beyond their boundaries, and why widespread access to collective knowledge does not produce equal benefits.
