5b51167fb0:bdb556254e68b6c5.title: Who Marries Whom? The Role of Segregation by Race and Class
5b51167fb0:bdb556254e68b6c5.author: info@aeaweb.org (Benjamin Goldman1, Jamie Gracie2 and Sonya R. Porter3 1 Cornell University (email: bgoldman@cornell.edu) 2 Harvard University (email: jgracie@g.harvard.edu) 3 US Census Bureau…
5b51167fb0:bdb556254e68b6c5.summary: American Economic Review 116 (10): 3623-3673 Abstract Americans rarely marry outside their race or class group, a pattern with well-documented implications for inequality and intergenerational mobility. Limited exposure may partly explain these low intergroup marriage rates. We instrument for exposure using variation in childhood neighborhoods based on whether other race and class groups had more opposite-sex children of similar age. Exposure increases interclass (high- and low-parent income) marriage but has no detectable effect on interracial (White and Black) marriage. A spatial marriage model predicts that residential segregation—one of many forms of exposure—accounts for more than one-third of marital sorting by class but less than 5 percent by race. (JEL J12, J15, J62, R23)

5b51167fb0:b43f16929197f266.title: Taxing Top Wealth: Migration Responses and Their Aggregate Economic Implications
5b51167fb0:b43f16929197f266.author: info@aeaweb.org (Katrine Jakobsen1, Henrik Kleven2, Jonas Kolsrud3, Camille Landais4 and Mathilde Munoz5 1 University of Copenhagen (email: katrinemariejakobsen@gmail.com) 2 Princeton University,…
5b51167fb0:b43f16929197f266.summary: American Economic Review 116 (10): 3674-3720 Abstract Using administrative data from Scandinavian countries, we provide evidence on international migration responses to wealth taxes and evaluate their aggregate economic implications. We find significant migration responses among the wealthy: A 1 percentage point increase in the top wealth tax rate decreases the stock of wealthy taxpayers by about 2 percent. A large fraction of the wealthy are business owners, and their businesses are negatively affected by owner out-migration. The aggregate effects are nevertheless modest: The migration responses to a 1 percentage point increase in the top wealth tax rate reduce employment by 0.02 percent, investments by 0.07 percent, and value added by 0.10 percent. (JEL D31, E22, E24, F22, H24, L26, K34)

5b51167fb0:da85f2a2d1dc685d.title: Racial Promotion Gaps
5b51167fb0:da85f2a2d1dc685d.author: info@aeaweb.org (Deepak Hegde1, Alexander Ljungqvist2 and Manav Raj3 1 New York University and NBER (email: dhegde@stern.nyu.edu) 2 Stockholm School of Economics, Swedish House of Finance, and CEPR…
5b51167fb0:da85f2a2d1dc685d.summary: American Economic Review 116 (10): 3721-3767 Abstract We study racial disparities in promotions in a setting in which promotions are formulaic: the US patent office. Using detailed administrative data that allow us to observe who is eligible for promotion when, we document that Black patent examiners experience delays in promotions they are entitled to, slowing their climb to the top of the career ladder by a year and reducing career earnings by 2.5 percent. Institutional features rule out statistical discrimination with accurate priors. Slow promotions even under Black supervisors argue against taste-based animus. Instead, the patterns fit models of belief-based discrimination. (JEL J15, J41, J71, M12, M51, O34)

5b51167fb0:4457dc712975ec95.title: Screening and Segmenting: A Consumer Surplus Perspective
5b51167fb0:4457dc712975ec95.author: info@aeaweb.org (Dirk Bergemann1, Tibor Heumann2 and Michael C. Wang3 1 Department of Economics, Yale University (email: dirk.bergemann@yale.edu) 2 Instituto de Economía, Pontificia Universidad…
5b51167fb0:4457dc712975ec95.summary: American Economic Review 116 (10): 3768-3801 Abstract We analyze consumer surplus when a monopolist can adjust both prices and product qualities across segments, engaging in secondand third-degree price discrimination simultaneously. We characterize the consumer-optimal segmentation and show that it has a striking structure: Consumers with the same value receive the same quality in every segment, though prices differ. Under mild conditions, any segmentation harms consumers if and only if demand is sufficiently more elastic than supply. Hence, potential benefits for consumers depend critically on demand and supply elasticities. These findings have implications for regulatory policy regarding price discrimination and market segmentation. (JEL D42, D83, K21, L12, L15)

5b51167fb0:a0b06843547e36d5.title: A Model of the Attention Economy: Data, Platforms, and Discovery
5b51167fb0:a0b06843547e36d5.author: info@aeaweb.org (Daniel Chen1 1 Assistant Professor of Economics, Princeton University (email: dtchen@princeton.edu))
5b51167fb0:a0b06843547e36d5.summary: American Economic Review 116 (10): 3802-3836 Abstract This paper develops a dynamic model of the attention economy featuring two interlinked markets: a product market, where consumers have limited awareness of firms, and an attention market, where platforms attract attention by investing in free services (e.g., social media, streaming, podcasts) and sell targeted ads using data on consumer preferences. The model provides a tractable framework in which platform investment, ad-driven discovery, product demand, and ad revenue are jointly determined. The effects of data and interoperability policies can reverse over time, platform quality may be inefficiently high or low, and the rise of data-rich digital advertising can coincide with a declining ad revenue-to-GDP ratio. (JEL D43, D44, D58, D83, L86, M37)

5b51167fb0:17af0ecaa5dc28ef.title: Fighting for Growth: Labor Scarcity and Technological Progress during the British Industrial Revolution
5b51167fb0:17af0ecaa5dc28ef.author: info@aeaweb.org (Hans-Joachim Voth1, Bruno Caprettini2 and Alex Trew3 1 University of Zurich and CEPR (voth@econ.uzh.ch) 2 University of St. Gallen and CEPR (bruno.caprettini@gmail.com) 3 University…
5b51167fb0:17af0ecaa5dc28ef.summary: American Economic Review 116 (10): 3837-3874 Abstract We establish a link between labor scarcity and the adoption of laborsaving technology in industrializing England. During the Napoleonic Wars, more than 10 percent of the male population served in the armed forces. Where recruitment was heavy, more machines economizing on labor were adopted. Naval recruitment, instrumented by warships' coastal access, provides exogenous variation in labor scarcity and suggests that the link between labor shortages and adoption is causal. Where mechanical skills were abundant, the impact of labor scarcity on adoption appears to be larger. (JEL J24, N13, N43, N63, N73, O14, O31)

5b51167fb0:5713354141b0f2d8.title: Social Push and the Direction of Innovation
5b51167fb0:5713354141b0f2d8.author: info@aeaweb.org (Elias Einiö1, Josh Feng2 and Xavier Jaravel3 1 VATT Institute for Economic Research (email: elias.einio@vatt.fi) 2 University of Utah (email: josh.feng@eccles.utah.edu) 3 London…
5b51167fb0:5713354141b0f2d8.summary: American Economic Review 116 (10): 3875-3909 Abstract What are the implications of unequal access to innovation careers for the direction of innovation and inequality? Leveraging novel linked datasets in the United States and Finland, we document that innovators create products more likely to be purchased by consumers like them in terms of gender, socioeconomic status, and age. Homophily exists both within narrow product categories and across industries and has been stable in recent decades. Incorporating this “social push” channel into a growth model, we estimate that unequal access to innovation careers has a large effect on cost of living inequality and long-run growth. (JEL D63, J16, L26, M13, O31, O33, O47)

5b51167fb0:66d365a090201a2f.title: Knowledge Spillovers, Competition, and Individual Careers
5b51167fb0:66d365a090201a2f.author: info@aeaweb.org (Thomas Cornelissen1, Christian Dustmann2 and Uta Schönberg3 1 Department of Economics, University of Essex, RF Berlin, and Institute for Employment Research (IAB) (email:…
5b51167fb0:66d365a090201a2f.summary: American Economic Review 116 (10): 3910-3941 Abstract Exposure to better peers in the workplace can influence career trajectories through two opposing channels: positively, via knowledge spillovers, and negatively, through competition for advancement. We disentangle these effects by studying untrained labor market entrants and distinguishing between coworkers in the same occupation with whom they are likely to compete versus those with whom they are unlikely to compete. We find robust evidence of persistent knowledge spillovers but also identify countervailing competition effects of comparable magnitude. Both effects are more pronounced for men than for women. (JEL D83, J16, J24, M53, M54, O33)

5b51167fb0:7cf1ce28f4d619bc.title: Truth Elicitation in a Nonstrategic Environment
5b51167fb0:7cf1ce28f4d619bc.author: info@aeaweb.org (Jacob Glazer1 and Ariel Rubinstein2 1 University of Warwick and Tel Aviv University (email: glazer@tauex.tau.ac.il) 2 Tel Aviv University and New York University (email:…
5b51167fb0:7cf1ce28f4d619bc.summary: American Economic Review 116 (10): 3942-3958 Abstract A principal decides which party deserves a prize. Only the parties observe the state that determines who is deserving. The principal gives each party a text describing the conditions under which that party deserves the prize and asks each to report the state. The parties are nonstrategic. Each activates a known cheating procedure whose outcome depends on the state and on the text. Implementation is achieved if, whenever the parties disagree, the liar is identified by the “one-way cheating principle”: The truthful party is the unique party who could not have produced his story had the rival's story been true. (JEL D82, D91)

5b51167fb0:140613fdcd625616.title: Presidential Address: Neighborhood Effects and Missing Markets for Opportunity
5b51167fb0:140613fdcd625616.author: info@aeaweb.org (Lawrence F. Katz1 1 Harvard University (email: lkatz@harvard.edu))
5b51167fb0:140613fdcd625616.summary: American Economic Review 116 (9): 3197-3222 Abstract Experimental and quasi-experimental studies show that childhood neighborhoods have substantial causal impacts on children's adult earnings and other long-term socioeconomic outcomes. Several market failures are likely to lead to excessive residential segregation by parental income and to an undersupply of mixed-income neighborhoods. Missing markets for opportunity originate in capital market imperfections for borrowing on children's future earnings, neighbor spillovers, behavioral biases, and housing search frictions. Customized housing mobility services combined with subsidized housing vouchers can help low-income families move to higher-opportunity areas. Place-based policies that create mixed-income neighborhoods appear to increase long-term outcomes for less-advantaged children. (JEL I12, I32, I38, J13, J15, R23, R38)

5b51167fb0:efb7cbbe3071ae07.title: Contextually Private Mechanisms
5b51167fb0:efb7cbbe3071ae07.author: info@aeaweb.org (Andreas Haupt1 and Zoë Hitzig2 1 Stanford Digital Economy Lab (email: h4upt@stanford.edu) 2 Harvard Society of Fellows (email: zhitzig@g.harvard.edu))
5b51167fb0:efb7cbbe3071ae07.summary: American Economic Review 116 (9): 3223-3262 Abstract A designer employs a dynamic protocol to elicit private information. Protocols produce a set of contextual privacy violations—information learned that may be superfluous given the context. A protocol is maximally contextually private if there is no protocol that produces a proper subset of the violations it produces, while implementing the choice rule. Contextual privacy violations arise when a choice rule makes some agents collectively, but not individually, pivotal. In auctions, designing for contextual privacy requires choosing an initial question posed to each agent and the order for querying agents. Ascending-join protocols are maximally contextually private for k-item Vickrey auctions. (JEL D44, D82)

5b51167fb0:1a15b1cd2416f9fe.title: Manipulation-Robust Prediction
5b51167fb0:1a15b1cd2416f9fe.author: info@aeaweb.org (Daniel Björkegren1, Joshua E. Blumenstock2 and Samsun Knight3 1 Columbia University (email: dan@bjorkegren.com) 2 UC Berkeley (email: jblumenstock@berkeley.edu) 3 University of…
5b51167fb0:1a15b1cd2416f9fe.summary: American Economic Review 116 (9): 3263-3293 Abstract An increasing number of decisions are guided by machine learning algorithms. But when consequential decisions are encoded in algorithms, individuals may strategically alter their behavior to achieve desired outcomes. This paper develops an empirical approach that adjusts decision algorithms to anticipate manipulation. By explicitly modeling incentives to manipulate, our approach produces decision rules that are stable under manipulation, even when the rules are fully transparent. We stress-test this approach through a large field experiment in Kenya. When implemented, linear strategy-robust decision rules outperform standard linear models such as LASSO. (JEL C45, C93, D12, D91, G51, O12, O16)

5b51167fb0:a1ffa58aef64f33d.title: Risk-Sharing Tests and Covariate Shocks: Drought, Floods, and Pests in Uganda
5b51167fb0:a1ffa58aef64f33d.author: info@aeaweb.org (Ethan Ligon1 1 University of California, Berkeley (email: ligon@berkeley.edu))
5b51167fb0:a1ffa58aef64f33d.summary: American Economic Review 116 (9): 3294-3329 Abstract Efficient risk sharing implies a simple factor structure for marginal utilities of expenditure (MUEs): Pareto weights divided by a common price. The standard approach infers MUEs from total expenditures, implicitly assuming homothetic preferences, unitary income elasticities, and identical price elasticities. Risk-sharing tests using total expenditures work for idiosyncratic shocks (budgets change, but not prices), but not “covariate” shocks (prices change). I describe all preferences that permit one to infer MUEs from expenditures and estimate nonhomothetic MUEs to test whether covariate shocks are shared efficiently in Uganda. This delivers sensible results; the standard approach suggests that droughts, floods, and pests are beneficial. (JEL D12, D81, O12, O13, Q12)

5b51167fb0:797852c7470100e9.title: Optimal Public Transportation Networks: Evidence from the World's Largest Bus Rapid Transit System in Jakarta
5b51167fb0:797852c7470100e9.author: info@aeaweb.org (Gabriel Kreindler1, Arya Gaduh2, Tilman Graff3, Rema Hanna4 and Benjamin A. Olken5 1 Harvard University (email: gkreindler@g.harvard.edu) 2 University of Arkansas (email:…
5b51167fb0:797852c7470100e9.summary: American Economic Review 116 (9): 3330-3379 Abstract Designing public transport networks involves trade-offs between coverage, service frequency, and direct service. We use the expansion of the bus system in Jakarta, Indonesia, to study these trade-offs. We analyze how new direct connections, changes in bus travel time, and wait-time reductions affect bus ridership and aggregate flows and estimate a transit network demand model by matching the route launch events. Commuters in Jakarta are 2–3 times more sensitive to wait time than bus time and inattentive to long routes. We develop a flexible framework to characterize optimal networks. A less concentrated network would increase ridership and commuter welfare. (JEL L92, L98, O18, R41, R42, R48)

5b51167fb0:07fc24e40491cd16.title: Corporate Tax Cuts, Firm Growth, and Workers' Earnings
5b51167fb0:07fc24e40491cd16.author: info@aeaweb.org (Patrick J. Kennedy1, Christine L. Dobridge2, Paul Landefeld3 and Jacob Mortenson4 1 UCLA, NBER, and JCT (email: pkennedy@econ.ucla.edu) 2 Federal Reserve Board (email:…
5b51167fb0:07fc24e40491cd16.summary: American Economic Review 116 (9): 3380-3422 Abstract We study the effects of the largest corporate income tax cut in US history on firms and workers. To identify causal effects, we use employer-employee matched tax records and event studies comparing similarly sized firms in the same industry that faced divergent tax changes due to their preexisting legal status. Tax cuts cause increases in firms' investment, sales, profits, employment, and payrolls, with earnings gains concentrated among highly paid workers. In the short run, 87 percent of private income gains flow to the top 10 percent of the income distribution. (JEL D22, D31, G31, H25, H32, J23, L25)

5b51167fb0:3ee043839f43fb4e.title: Marriage, Fertility, and Cultural Integration in Italy
5b51167fb0:3ee043839f43fb4e.author: info@aeaweb.org (Alberto Bisin1 and Giulia Tura2 1 New York University (email: alberto.bisin@nyu.edu) 2 LUISS University (email: gtura@luiss.it))
5b51167fb0:3ee043839f43fb4e.summary: American Economic Review 116 (9): 3423-3463 Abstract We study cultural integration as an equilibrium outcome of marital matching along cultural and education lines and intrahousehold investment decisions regarding fertility and cultural socialization. Our model allows us to identify cultural-ethnic-group-specific investment parameters and spousal preferences for marital matching. Structural estimates reveal a strong demand to preserve cultural identity on the part of immigrants and limited acceptance of the immigrants' cultural diversity on the part of natives. Furthermore, these estimates reveal a substantial heterogeneity of the parental value of children's education across cultures. Nonetheless, our estimates simulate substantial—though heterogeneous—cultural integration rates across immigrant groups. (JEL D13, J12, J13, J15, Z13)

5b51167fb0:26e7d435f0796a13.title: Defying Distance? The Provision of Medical Services in the Digital Age
5b51167fb0:26e7d435f0796a13.author: info@aeaweb.org (Amanda Dahlstrand1 1 University of Zurich (email: amanda.dahlstrand@econ.uzh.ch))
5b51167fb0:26e7d435f0796a13.summary: American Economic Review 116 (9): 3464-3509 Abstract Digital platforms reduce geographic frictions, enabling better matching between service providers and users. I quantify reallocation gains in Swedish online health care, using nationwide time-conditional random assignment between patients and physicians. Matching high-risk patients with doctors effective at reducing Emergency Room visits lowers such visits by 4.4 percent (SE 1.3); reallocations also reduce Counter-Guideline antibiotics by 3.1 percent (1.4). I find limited trade-offs in matching; horizontal differentiation among doctors and varied patient needs allow improvement in multiple outcomes simultaneously. Efficiency-enhancing reallocations also affect equity. The findings highlight the potential for care reorganization aligning provider heterogeneity with patient needs when geographic constraints are lifted. (JEL C78, H51, I11, I13, I14, I18)

5b51167fb0:221f12c25326ebda.title: The Environmental Bias of Corporate Income Taxation
5b51167fb0:221f12c25326ebda.author: info@aeaweb.org (Luigi Iovino1, Thorsten Martin2 and Julien Sauvagnat3 1 Bocconi University (email: luigi.iovino@unibocconi.it) 2 Frankfurt School of Finance and Management (email: t.martin@fs.de) 3…
5b51167fb0:221f12c25326ebda.summary: American Economic Review 116 (9): 3510-3551 Abstract We study the relationship between corporate income taxation and carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions in the United States. We show CO2-intensive firms benefit more from the tax advantage of debt and pay lower income taxes on their capital income. Building on these new facts, we provide evidence that a cut in the corporate income tax rate leads to a larger expansion of clean firms. We develop a multisector general equilibrium model that accounts for our evidence and quantify the impact of corporate tax reforms on aggregate emissions. A policy that eliminates the tax advantage of debt could reduce aggregate emissions without affecting GDP. (JEL D22, G32, H25, H32, Q52, Q54, Q58)

5b51167fb0:273a7079633c9788.title: Rationing by Race
5b51167fb0:273a7079633c9788.author: info@aeaweb.org (Manasvini Singh1 and Atheendar Venkataramani2 1 Carnegie Mellon University and NBER (email: msingh01@cmu.edu) 2 University of Pennsylvania and NBER (email:…
5b51167fb0:273a7079633c9788.summary: American Economic Review 116 (9): 3552-3585 Abstract We document how deepening resource scarcity results in rationing on the basis of race in a high-stakes setting: health care. Using detailed, time stamped data on 107,000 inpatient admissions to a large health system, we find that in-hospital mortality increases for Black but not White patients as hospitals reach capacity. These findings are not explained by differential patient selection. We identify rationing by wait times as a mechanism, documenting that sicker Black patients wait longer for care than healthier White patients at almost all capacity levels. Text analysis of unstructured clinical notes reveals rationing of provider effort as another mechanism. (JEL I11, I12, I14, J15)

5b51167fb0:b142b734d632b9cc.title: Intergenerational Impacts of Secondary Education: Experimental Evidence from Ghana
5b51167fb0:b142b734d632b9cc.author: info@aeaweb.org (Esther Duflo1, Pascaline Dupas2, Elizabeth Spelke3 and Mark Walsh4 1 MIT and Collège de France (email: eduflo@mit.edu) 2 Princeton University (email: pdupas@princeton.edu) 3 Harvard…
5b51167fb0:b142b734d632b9cc.summary: American Economic Review 116 (9): 3586-3621 Abstract We provide experimental evidence on the intergenerational impacts of secondary education subsidies in a low-income context, leveraging a randomized controlled trial and 15-year longitudinal follow-up. Secondary school scholarships delay fertility, reduce unwanted pregnancies, and change partner selection. Under-one mortality is reduced by half. We also document cognitive development gains of 0.24 standard deviations of test scores by age five among children of female scholarship recipients. Means-tested secondary school scholarships are a high-return investment, with a conservatively estimated US$4.1 in benefits for each US$1 the policy would cost the government in the long run. (JEL H52, I12, I21, I26, J13, J16, O15)

Consuni approves granting the title of Doctor Honoris Causa to Marilda Sotomayor "The University Council (Consuni) approved, by acclaim, the granting of the title of Doctor Honoris Causa to the professor and mathematics Marilda Antonia de Oliveira Sotomayor. ... "Marilda Sotomayor is recognized for her contribution to Game Theory and Matching Theory, an area dedicated to the study of allocation mechanisms in two-sided markets. The opinion of the Special Commission highlighted its contribution to the consolidation of this field of research in Brazil and its international projection. "Graduated in Mathematics from the Federal University of Rio de Janeiro (UFRJ), Marilda completed a master’s degree at the Institute of Pure and Applied Mathematics (Impa) and a doctorate from the Pontifical Catholic University of Rio de Janeiro (PUC-Rio), in partnership with Impa. During the postdoctoral degree at the University of California, Berkeley, she worked with David Gale, one of the founders of Matching Theory. "Among her main contributions is the book Two-Sided Matching: A Study in Game-Theoretic Modeling and Analysis, published in 1990 in co-authorship with Alvin Roth. The work received the Lanchester Prize and became an international reference in the area. Marilda is also a member of the Brazilian Academy of Sciences and the American Academy of Arts and Sciences and has received, among other distinctions, the 2016 TWAS Award. "The proposal to grant the title was presented by Professor Maurício Bugarin to the Department of Economics (ECO/Face) and encamped by the Faculty of Economics, Administration, Accounting and Public Policy Management (Face)." ###########

21113a7a19:76ed32eea3176b4f.title: How successfully have military measures limited the supply of cocaine?
21113a7a19:76ed32eea3176b4f.author: Al Roth (noreply@blogger.com)
21113a7a19:76ed32eea3176b4f.summary: There are two ways of measuring the success of military measures to limit the supply of cocaine. There's the military measure of how many people are killed and how much cocaine is confiscated. And there's the economic measure of how much cocaine is available to consumers, at what price and quality. The WSJ has the story (of plunging prices and rising quality): Why U.S. Airstrikes Are Failing to Stop the Global Cocaine Boom Smugglers are shifting routes and using new tactics to evade military targeting, resulting in record supplies, plunging prices and high purity in the U.S. and Europe by Juan Forero | "BUENAVENTURA, Colombia—The Trump administration’s bombing campaign against cocaine-smuggling speedboats is starting to have an impact on the global drug trade—but not necessarily in a good way. ... " Record supplies of cocaine still arrive in the U.S., Europe and as far away as Australia every day, cheaper and purer than they’ve been in decades , said law-enforcement officials across four continents. " President Trump has celebrated the airstrikes, noting his administration has “made tremendous strides in stopping the flow of illegal drugs into our country.” In the past 13 months, American military drones and aircraft have destroyed more than 70 vessels, killing nearly 240 crew members and depriving criminal groups of $1.5 billion in cocaine, according to U.S. officials. “The drugs coming in by sea are down by 97%,” Trump said in June. “We’re trying to figure out who the 3% are, because they are the bravest people on earth.” ... "The scale of the trade is evident on the streets of drug-consuming countries, where supply is outstripping demand to the point that prices are plunging. In Miami, wholesale cocaine sold for about $16,500 a kilogram this summer, well below the historical $22,000 to $25,000 range. Similarly, European prices have plummeted from $45,000 to as low as $16,000 a kilogram in some cities. "In both markets, purity remains remarkably high, sometimes…

21113a7a19:0b3e864f26759c4c.title: Kidney exchange in India at a national scale: a growing consensus
21113a7a19:0b3e864f26759c4c.author: Al Roth (noreply@blogger.com)
21113a7a19:0b3e864f26759c4c.summary: There's growing consensus in India on moving towards a nationwide kidney exchange program. Kute V, Kumar A, Balwani M et al. Operational guidelines for kidney swap transplantation in India: an ISOT-NOTTO Delphi consensus The Lancet Regional Health – Southeast Asia, 2026; 0 Among the consensus recommendations is this one, which summarizes the general positive tone adopted for national kidney exchange. "Each transplant center should initiate and expand swap transplantation, given that it is legal, cost-effective, yields better outcomes, and can help prevent unethical commercial transplants by improving access. Multicentric swap transplantation programmes should roll out in phases: start with intra-city exchanges, then intra-state, and eventually inter-state and national collaborations. This phased approach ensures growing scale is matched with operational readiness, providing safe, equitable, and efficient transplants across regions."

21113a7a19:c6f9ebdacc9b1381.author: Al Roth (noreply@blogger.com)
21113a7a19:c6f9ebdacc9b1381.summary: Dr. Steve Woodle, one of the pioneers of kidney exchange, is being honored in Cincinnati. You can read of his many distinctions below, but here's a striking one: he is the " the first liver transplant recipient to perform a liver transplant ." 2026 Daniel Drake Medals The University of Cincinnati College of Medicine’s highest honor E. Steve Woodle, MD E. Steve Woodle, MD Woodle, professor of surgery and the William A. Altemeier endowed chair in surgery at the College of Medicine, is a multiorgan transplant surgeon and transplant immunologist who has spent more than four decades advancing the understanding of organ rejection and pioneering immunosuppressive therapies that have reshaped transplantation. Earlier in his career at the University of Chicago, he performed a liver transplant on a 10-day-old infant, setting a Guinness World Record for the youngest liver transplant recipient. He joined the College of Medicine in 1999 and directed the Division of Transplantation for nearly two decades, building an internationally recognized program of clinical and research excellence. In 2001, he performed Ohio’s first allogeneic islet transplant for type 1 diabetes. After undergoing his own liver transplant in 2003, Woodle returned to the operating room and became the first liver transplant recipient to perform a liver transplant. Woodle has helped originate several therapeutic approaches now considered standard in transplantation. As a fellow, he conceived the genetic re-engineering of OKT3, the first FDA-approved monoclonal antibody — work later developed into teplizumab (Tzield), which the FDA approved in 2022 as the first immunomodulatory therapy for type 1 diabetes. He was the first investigator to introduce plasma cell-targeted therapy for a non-malignant human disease, using proteasome inhibitors to treat antibody-mediated rejection in kidney transplant recipients. 21113a7a19:a7d807e7d8608906.title: The once and future market for prostitution in Rhode Island
21113a7a19:a7d807e7d8608906.author: Al Roth (noreply@blogger.com)
21113a7a19:a7d807e7d8608906.summary: Kim Krawiec , the great legal scholar of repugnant transactions, has written that rare (almost never seen) book review that extends the empirical study of an important, well-studied social science event, namely Rhode Island's experience of legal prostitution. It provides an illuminating followup to the germinal paper by Cunningham and Shah. (Prostitution in R.I. is one of the controversial markets covered in Moral Economics , and I believe Krawiec's book review is headed for a forthcoming symposium on the book in Œconomia ­­.) The Smallest State's Big Experiment by Kimberly D. Krawiec October 09, 2026 Abstract Rhode Island’s accidental decriminalization of prostitution in 1980 is typically told as the story of a legal change that went unnoticed for more than two decades. This review of Alvin Roth’s latest book, Moral Economics, challenges that standard account and explores its implications for Roth’s argument that markets need social support to flourish. Drawing on court records, contemporaneous news reports, arrest statistics, and legislative proceedings, I show that the statutory change was noticed almost immediately. Prostitution-related arrests continued, not because police and prosecutors were ignorantly arresting and charging sex workers and clients under a statute that no longer existed, but because the legal system adapted using tools – primarily the loitering prohibition that survived the 1980 rewrite – that have long been used to police behavior and individuals considered repugnant. After a 2003 judicial ruling closed an important enforcement avenue against indoor sex work and vaulted the market into the open, a coalition formed around trafficking concerns that eventually paved the way for recriminalization in 2009. Rhode Island’s accidental experiment with decriminalized sex work provided neither the deliberately designed regulatory framework nor the political backing that could build the type of social support that Roth insists (correctly, in my view)…

Canada Halts Plan to Allow Medically Assisted Death for the Mentally Ill. People who have mental illness alone will not qualify for assisted death, but patients who have other conditions and expect to have a cognitive decline can make an advanced request. By Vjosa Isai "Canada will reverse its plan to allow people whose sole condition is a mental illness to seek medically assisted death, the government announced on Wednesday, abandoning a move to expand access to these patients. “ While there is not a perfect consensus on this issue , we believe this is the correct approach,” Sean Fraser, the minister of justice, told reporters on Parliament Hill. "A law, introduced under the former Prime Minister Justin Trudeau, that allowed people with intolerable suffering from incurable mental health conditions to access a medically assisted death was initially poised to take effect in March 2023. Access for these patients was postponed for a year after public and some medical-community concerns that the existing system was not yet prepared to evaluate applications from these patients. In March 2024, the government delayed again, this time until March 2027, pending reviews by a panel of experts. "With the clock ticking toward that deadline, Mr. Fraser said the government “very recently” formalized its stance and that Canadians can soon expect parliament to pass legislation that will indefinitely bar people whose sole medical condition is a mental disorder from seeking medically assisted death. 21113a7a19:90ee420ba69365a8.summary: Here's an interview with Harvard Professor Sarah Richardson about her recent article raising concerns about menstrual tracking apps. "These apps are marketed as wellness and medical tools, but there are no protections on the data. Data is often sold, raising concerns for reproductive autonomy and privacy. Menstrual apps are unique compared to other kinds of digital trackers because they can expose reproductive and gender status. "It is possible for there to be misuse of this data. This was deeply scrutinized after the Dobbs decision a couple of years ago with many scholars recommending that people not use these tracking apps, because there had been explicit threats made by regulators to try to access that data for use in criminal prosecution. "Menstrual status can be used to give evidence of reproductive status. If the use of one of these apps exposed somebody as having been pregnant and then no longer being pregnant, for example, that could potentially be, in some jurisdictions, used either to discriminate against them or to implicate them criminally under laws that are meant to restrict abortion. The first 100 cases of organ donation after euthanasia in the Netherlands: lessons from preliminary experiences. BMC Med Ethics (2026). https://doi.org/10.1186/s12910-026-01590-5 "Background Organ donation after euthanasia (ODE) is an evolving, patient-initiated procedure in the Netherlands. While it gives meaning to donors at the end-of-life, it introduces complex ethical and practical challenges for healthcare professionals. This study aims to describe the clinical characteristics and donation outcomes of the first 100 ODE procedures in the Netherlands, while outlining the practical and ethical dilemmas encountered. Methods A retrospective analysis was performed on prospectively collected data from the first 100 ODE procedures conducted between September 2012 and February 2023. To gain deeper insight into practical experiences and ethical themes, these data were discussed with organ donation coordinators and intensivists involved in the procedures. The analysis focused on clinical characteristics and donation outcomes, as on ethical and practical challenges. Results Neurodegenerative disorders were the primary underlying cause of suffering (52%), followed by psychiatric conditions (31%). The first 100 procedures resulted in 408 transplanted organs. Most procedures were performed in intensive care units, with general practitioners performing euthanasia. Key ethical and practical challenges included the tension between clinical protocols (e.g., fasting) and patient comfort, the medicalisation of the dying process through invasive monitoring, and the logistical barriers of starting ODE from home (ODEH). (It appears only to have reviewed papers that were also published in English.) The title summarizes the conclusion, that the market aligns with the goals of Islamic law. Faisal, Ahmad, Abdul Khakim Mahfud Zubaidi, Ahmad Nizar Zuhdi Al Hakimi, and Roya Goldoust. “ The Iranian government’s efforts to facilitate foundation-led kidney donation align with the Maqāsid al-Sharī’ah .” Al-Madina: Journal of Islamic Law 1, no. 1 (2026): 28–48. Abstract The issue of kidney transplantation, particularly through compensated living-unrelated donors, represents a complex intersection of medical necessity, ethical debate, and international governance. Iran is unique in legally regulating compensated kidney donation, aiming to address the chronic shortage of transplantable organs while providing structured financial incentives to donors. This study analyzes Iran’s kidney donation system through the lens of maqāsid al-sharī’ah, emphasizing the objective of hifz al-nafs (preservation of life), to evaluate both the ethical legitimacy and life-saving effectiveness of the policy. Employing a qualitative-descriptive approach, the research synthesizes empirical evidence on donor demographics, motivations, compensation mechanisms, and clinical outcomes, alongside normative Islamic ethical considerations and international standards such as the WHO Guiding Principles and the Declaration of Istanbul. Findings reveal that while Iran’s system significantly enhances patient survival and fulfills the core goal of hifz al-nafs, donor participation is heavily influenced by economic necessity, raising ethical concerns about voluntariness, long-term welfare, and equitable access. Moreover, the system’s interaction with foreign patients highlights challenges in cross-border governance and the potential for transplant tourism. The study contributes…

21113a7a19:8562b73267220857.author: Al Roth (noreply@blogger.com)
21113a7a19:8562b73267220857.summary: As LLMs become increasingly important, we're starting to see experiments that explore their psychology. (I expect that Susan Calvin, who was Isaac Asimov's fictional robopsychologist from the1950 short story collection I Robot , will soon have scientists following in her footsteps.) Note that experiments intended to explore A.I. psychology need not necessarily resemble those intended to explore human psychology. Here's an example, from the journal Artificial Intelligence and the Law: Human realignment: An empirical study of LLMs as legal decision-aids in moral dilemmas by Christoph Engel · Yoan Hermstrüwer · Alison Kim Abstract: Recent advances in AI make it conceivable to delegate legal decision-making to machines, or to enhance human adjudication through AI assistance. Using classic normative conflicts — the trolley problem and comparable moral dilemmas — as a proof of concept, we examine the alignment between AI legal reasoning and human judgment. In our baseline experiment, we find a pronounced mismatch between decisions made by GPT and those of human subjects. This misalignment raises substantive concerns for AI-powered legal decision-aids. We investigate whether explicit normative guidance can address this misalignment, with mixed results. GPT-3.5 is susceptible to such intervention, but frequently refuses to decide when faced with a moral dilemma. GPT-4 is outright utilitarian, and essentially ignores the instruction to decide on deontological grounds. GPT-o3-mini faithfully implements this instruction, but is unwilling to balance deontological and utilitarian concerns if instructed to do so. We replicate the experiment with four LLMs from different providers. Claude-sonnet-4.6 comes closest to human respondents. Gemini-2.5-flash-lite is most sensitive to normative instructions. 21113a7a19:c56640781616b6c7.summary: Transplants of organs from genetically modified pigs to humans is making progress, but pig organs haven't yet survived long enough to be a viable substitute for human organs. Kidneys are a good experimental organ to work with, because when the pig organ fails, the patient can go back on dialysis (and continue to wait for a deceased-donor organ transplant). But if pig organs can last long enough, they might replace dialysis. The first pig-organ recipient to go straight to a human organ transplant has now been reported, in a press release accompanying the case report. Below are both the press release and the case report. Early cellular rejection resolved with treatment, whereas later graft failure was associated with microvascular injury progressing to thrombotic microangiopathy despite a negative donor-specific crossmatch, supporting the possibility that mechanisms beyond conventional antibody-mediated rejection contributed to late graft injury. 21113a7a19:2c743f5c371780f9.title: How to Get Away with Merger in a Dialysis Duopoly by T.G. Wollman
21113a7a19:2c743f5c371780f9.author: Al Roth (noreply@blogger.com)
21113a7a19:2c743f5c371780f9.summary: Here's a paper featured by Microeconomic Insights, which shows that in the highly concentrated dialysis market, in which prices are mostly federally regulated, mergers reduce competition on quality. Thomas G. Wollmann: How to Get Away with Merger: Stealth Consolidation and Its Effects on US Dialysis "This paper studies premerger notification of US dialysis acquisitions from 1996 to 2017. Like many industries, dialysis has consolidated rapidly. During this period, thousands of facilities changed ownership, yet only half were reported to federal antitrust authorities. Unlike most industries, dialysis prices are mostly set by the government, so acquisitions of rival facilities reduce the incentive to compete on quality. Since patients are often already in poor health, preventing stealth consolidation could save lives. The study combines data on market structure, antitrust enforcement, and patient health. I begin by describing patterns in the data. Next, I estimate a structural model of dialysis competition, enforcement, and agency costs. Finally, I use the estimates to predict what would have happened had all dialysis mergers proposed during the study period been reportable. Three main findings emerge. Premerger notification is critical to effective antitrust enforcement. All else equal, exemption reduces the likelihood of enforcement by about 90%. Exempt acquisitions that concentrate ownership degrade quality, as evidenced by higher postmerger hospitalization and mortality rates. The benefits of expanding premerger notification exceed the costs by orders of magnitude. This reflects the deterrence effect of antitrust enforcement (i.e., rivals won’t try to merge if they know their deal will be blocked) as well as the efficiency of the Federal Trade Commission (FTC), which polices billions of dollars of dialysis transactions with very few resources."

2f5fdda6a0:11279647bd188980.title: Household Finance at the Origin: Home Ownership as a Cultural Heritage from Agriculture
2f5fdda6a0:11279647bd188980.author: Vuillemey, Guillaume
2f5fdda6a0:11279647bd188980.summary: I show that home ownership decisions across countries and individuals are shaped by a cultural heritage from agriculture. For centuries, dominant assets in preindustrial economies were either land or cattle. Consequently, the type of farming prevailing locally shaped preferences and beliefs about the relative value of immovable and movable assets. This cultural heritage had long-lasting consequences. Today, individuals originating from societies with a history of crop agriculture—where the dominant asset was land—are more likely to be homeowners. For identification, I rely both on home ownership decisions of second-generation immigrants in the United States and on an instrument.

2f5fdda6a0:ba9aa8468033340e.title: Star Firms, Information Spillovers, and Predictable Industry-Level Outcomes
2f5fdda6a0:ba9aa8468033340e.author: Rantala, Ville
2f5fdda6a0:ba9aa8468033340e.summary: We study the aggregate impact of information spillovers emerging from industry star firms. Changes in stars’ relative earnings growth predict future earnings growth, consensus earnings surprises, and job postings of same-industry nonstar firms. Star-firm performance also predicts industry-level GDP and employment growth. Price markup and innovation spillovers are potential channels underlying these patterns. Our results further show that this performance predictability is not fully incorporated into nonstars’ stock prices. A long–short portfolio based on star firms’ earnings growth earns an annualized 6-factor alpha of 8.7%. Together, our findings provide consistent evidence of the economic importance of star firms.

2f5fdda6a0:ab9e990a8b8dc381.title: Why Do Bank Boards Have Risk Committees?
2f5fdda6a0:ab9e990a8b8dc381.author: Ye, Zhongxia (Shelly)
2f5fdda6a0:ab9e990a8b8dc381.summary: While the Dodd–Frank Act (DFA) mandates board risk committees for large banks, we argue that such committees do not benefit all banks. Banks forced by the DFA to adopt a board risk committee do not experience a reduction in risk following adoption. In contrast, banks that voluntarily established risk committees before the DFA exhibit lower risk, especially when these committees possess greater risk expertise. Using unique interview data, we find that board risk committees serve as active monitors rather than merely rubber-stamping management proposals. However, regulatory-mandated tasks limit their monitoring role.

2f5fdda6a0:e400321c9bbca311.title: Personal Financial Information Presentation and Consumer Spending
2f5fdda6a0:e400321c9bbca311.author: Levi, Yaron
2f5fdda6a0:e400321c9bbca311.summary: We study whether information design influences consumer behavior in a randomized field experiment with users of an online account aggregation app. Participants received a personalized index representing their net worth as a lifetime monthly cash flow. The presentation of this index varied across treatments in its framing and the salience of its display. Consumers exposed to a consumption-oriented frame and a salient comparison of the index with their past spending reduced discretionary spending. These findings show that minor variations in information presentation can significantly affect financial behavior, highlighting the power of design in promoting saving and informing policy and regulation.
